solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Father’s behind packing case filled with earth (9)

indicators.note: a case filled with something has it inside, so E goes within CRATE

blocks.note: to be behind someone is to back them, to be pro
a crate is a packing case
E is the standard abbreviation for earth

annotation.surface: Someone's dad is round the back, packing a crate with soil.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Father' is a verb here, and 'behind' means supporting, not at the back.
annotation.definitionFit: Used as a verb, to father is the male part in producing offspring, a plain synonym.

entries.clue: Musician played quietly in supporting part (5)

indicators.note: the letter for quietly is placed in the supporting part, so it sits inside

blocks.note: a pier is a pillar supporting a bridge or arch

annotation.surface: A performer playing softly while taking a supporting role.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Supporting part' reads as a minor role in a show; it is a piece of architecture.
annotation.definitionFit: The bagpipe player is the classic example, a definition by example of a musician.

entries.clue: Were Peary and Henson first to be so delighted? (2,3,2,3,5)

definitions.text: Were Peary and Henson first to be so delighted?

blocks.note: Peary and Henson claimed to be first to the North Pole, the literal top of the globe
asks for an idiom meaning overjoyed that also fits where they stood

annotation.surface: A question about how two polar explorers felt.
annotation.walkthrough: Robert Peary and Matthew Henson claimed to reach the North Pole in 1909. The question mark asks you to read the idiom literally.
annotation.definitionFit: The idiom means elated, and the explorers were also standing on the top of the globe.

entries.clue: Back together about eleven in Manchester or Leeds? (8)

blocks.note: Manchester United and Leeds United are football teams, and a team is an eleven

annotation.surface: Wondering whether a group reunion involves a football team from the north of England.
annotation.walkthrough: A football side has eleven players, so 'eleven' is a team; both clubs named are United.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: people who have been apart and meet again are back together.

entries.clue: Always embracing jolly host (4)

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in your arms, so the word for always wraps round the jolly

blocks.note: ay (or aye) is an old word for always
a jolly is old slang for a Royal Marine, RM

annotation.surface: Someone forever hugging a cheerful party host.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Host' is not someone giving a party but the old sense of a great multitude.
annotation.definitionFit: An older, mostly literary sense: a host was an armed force, as in 'the heavenly host'.

entries.clue: Stuck here or travelling back from Mars? (10)

blocks.note: unable to leave the ground or this planet

annotation.surface: An astronaut stranded, or heading home from the red planet.
annotation.walkthrough: The second meaning splits the word: a craft heading back from Mars is bound for Earth.
annotation.definitionFit: The word means tied to the ground, and read in two halves it means heading towards Earth.

entries.clue: Pulled in by severe current, pop up again? (5)

indicators.note: the answer has been pulled into the words that follow, so it lies inside them

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

annotation.surface: Someone dragged under by a riptide wonders whether they will surface again.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a swimmer in a riptide, so 'pop up again' reads as bobbing to the surface.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something that recurs happens or turns up once more.

entries.clue: Fibres are cut up with doubled force by climbing sloth (6)

definitions.note: raffia is a mass noun for the fibre; the clue uses the plural

indicators.note: a word that is cut is shortened, so ARE loses its last letter
in a down answer, up means the letters read from bottom to top
to double something is to make two of it, so the letter for force appears twice
something climbing goes upward, so in a down answer the sloth reads backwards

blocks.note: the word ARE with its last letter cut off
the ai is the three-toed sloth

annotation.surface: Rope fibres chewed up by a sloth pulling hard as it climbs a tree.
annotation.walkthrough: The ai, a sloth, is a crossword regular because it has two letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Raffia is the fibre stripped from palm leaves, used for weaving and tying, so a plain synonym.

entries.clue: Criminal case legal hurdle for statesman (7,2,6)

indicators.note: criminal means crooked, and crooked letters are bent out of their order

annotation.surface: A prosecution stalled by a point of law before a politician can be tried.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a courtroom story, and 'Criminal case' reads as one phrase; split it, and 'Criminal' is the instruction while 'case' joins the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: de Gaulle led Free France in the war and later became French President.

entries.clue: Checks taxes — not for the first time? (9)

blocks.note: taxes = strains, as in 'taxes your patience'

annotation.surface: Someone inspecting tax bills they have seen before.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Checks' and 'taxes' both look like money words, but here they are verbs: holds back, and puts a strain on.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to check an advance is to hold it back.

entries.clue: Novel issued again following delays (3,3,4,5)

blocks.note: to put out is to issue or publish
to flag is to slacken or lag

annotation.surface: A book reissued after hold-ups at the printers.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Issued again' looks like one phrase about a reprint; it is two chunks.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: it is Evelyn Waugh's 1942 satirical wartime novel.

entries.clue: Material broadcast in resort (6)

blocks.note: to air a programme is to broadcast it

annotation.surface: Fabric being shown on television at a holiday resort.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Resort' reads as a seaside town but is a verb, as in resorting to the bar.
annotation.definitionFit: A slightly formal sense: to repair to a place is to go there, just as you resort to it.

entries.clue: Hard feeding budgie? It might grab you! (8)

indicators.note: feeding a bird puts something into it, so the letter for hard goes inside

blocks.note: a budgie is a bird that trills; the question mark flags it as an example

annotation.surface: Warning someone that a budgie is hard to feed because it might bite.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: a gripping book grabs its reader, not a finger.
annotation.definitionFit: Idiom: a gripping story is said to grab you, so the definition describes what a thriller does.

entries.clue: Strict regime? Family perish in street after a time (6,4)

indicators.note: the word for perish is placed in the street, so it sits inside ST
what comes after follows in the answer, so the family and street go behind A T

annotation.surface: A harsh government under which a whole family dies in the road.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Strict regime' sounds political; the question mark hints it is a diet regime.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Atkins diet is a strict low-carbohydrate eating regime.

entries.clue: Turning aside cast in Cold Feet (10)

indicators.note: to cast is to throw, and thrown letters land in a new order

annotation.surface: An actor in the TV drama Cold Feet turning away.
annotation.walkthrough: Cold Feet is a British TV comedy-drama, so 'cast in' reads as its actors; 'in' belongs to the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: deflection is the act of turning something off its course.

entries.clue: One close to spies in Washington misses leaks (9)

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so this takes the last letter of spies
one and the spy letter are put in Washington, so they sit inside DC

blocks.note: to miss a chance is to lose it

annotation.surface: An intelligence insider in Washington fails to stop leaks.
annotation.walkthrough: 'One close to spies' reads as an insider; 'misses' and 'leaks' are verbs, not nouns.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to leak secrets is to disclose them.

entries.clue: Wine’s seen better days — case chucked away (4)

indicators.note: a word's case is its outer letters, and chucking it away leaves the inside

blocks.note: past it = seen better days; its first and last letters are the case

annotation.surface: A bottle of wine gone off, so the crate is thrown out.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Case' looks like a wine case; it is the outside of PAST IT, leaving the Italian sparkler.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Asti is a sparkling wine from Piedmont in Italy.

entries.clue: Sends up a perch to be used in cooked dishes (8)

indicators.note: an ingredient used in a dish goes inside it, so A ROD goes into PIES

blocks.note: a perch, or rod, is an old unit of length

annotation.surface: A perch, the fish, going into a pie.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Perch' is the fish in the surface but the old measure in the wordplay: a perch is the same length as a rod, 5.5 yards.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: to send something up is to mock it by imitation.

entries.clue: Penny leaving store takes in old London area (4)

indicators.note: the penny leaves the store, so its letter is taken out
to take something in is to hold it inside, so what is left wraps round O

annotation.surface: Penny walks out of a shop in an old part of London.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Penny' reads as a woman's name; it is the coin, abbreviated p.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Soho is a district of London's West End known for nightlife.

entries.clue: Rugby side welcomes more cultivated people working with Pride? (4-6)

indicators.note: to welcome someone is to take them in, so the rugby side holds the other word

blocks.note: the British and Irish Lions are a touring rugby team

annotation.surface: A rugby team welcoming refined people who work for the Pride festival.
annotation.walkthrough: The capital P steers you to Pride marches; a pride is a group of lions.
annotation.definitionFit: A pun on a collective noun: a pride is a group of lions, which is what lion-tamers work with.

entries.clue: An old Shakespearean corporal’s assumed name (6)

blocks.note: Corporal Nym appears in Henry V and The Merry Wives of Windsor

annotation.surface: Asking what a Shakespearean soldier's pseudonym was.
annotation.walkthrough: The corporal's name is the whole last chunk; the possessive just joins it to the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A rare word: an anonym is a pseudonym, a name used to hide one's identity.

entries.clue: Obscenity one’s always banned in lies about Widnes (8)

indicators.note: something banned is kept out, so the letter for one is removed
about means around, so the shortened lies wrap round the shortened town

blocks.note: I = one, removed wherever it appears

annotation.surface: A complaint about indecency: dirty rumours about the town of Widnes should be banned.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Always' tells you I goes from both words, not just one. Widnes is an industrial town in Cheshire.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: lewd talk is obscene, so lewdness and obscenity name the same quality.

entries.clue: Revolutionary prison in Low Country (6)

indicators.note: a revolution is a turn, so the prison is turned round
the turned prison is put in the word for low, so it sits inside MOO

blocks.note: to low is to moo, like a cow

annotation.surface: A rebel jail in the Netherlands.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Low Country' reads as the Low Countries, but 'Low' is the cow's noise.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Monaco is a tiny sovereign principality on the Riviera.

entries.clue: Maybe G8 leaders to end talks after month? (5)

indicators.note: leaders go at the front, so take the first letter of each word
what comes after follows in the answer, so ET goes behind the month

blocks.note: Oct is the calendar abbreviation for October

annotation.surface: Heads of the G8 nations wanting to wrap up a summit after a month.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Leaders' looks like presidents and prime ministers, but it asks for first letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example, flagged by 'Maybe': the G8 was a group of eight nations.

entries.clue: American good with academician in Asian location (4)

blocks.note: RA = Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts

annotation.surface: A decent American and a scholar meeting somewhere in Asia.
annotation.walkthrough: The three short chunks are all standard abbreviations.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Agra, home of the Taj Mahal, is a city in northern India.

entries.clue: Withdrawn sort given toil, upset, faced with therapist (9,6)

indicators.note: something upset is knocked over, so its letters fall into a new order
a face is at the front, so the therapist goes before the rest

blocks.note: shrink is slang for a psychiatrist

annotation.surface: A timid person, burdened with work and distressed, sent to see a therapist.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Given' looks like a link word, but it is part of the fodder; the therapist comes first in the answer though last in the clue.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: a shrinking violet is a shy, retiring person, likened to the modest flower.

entries.clue: Thus perform mass in wicked place (5)

annotation.surface: A priest celebrating Mass in a den of iniquity.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mass' is the physics symbol, not the church service.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: in Genesis, Sodom is the city destroyed for its wickedness.

entries.clue: Passing tennis shot after cunning returns (9)

indicators.note: something shot is wrecked, so its letters are all over the place
what comes after follows in the answer, so the scrambled tennis goes behind
something that returns goes back, so the word for cunning reads backwards

annotation.surface: A passing shot at tennis, played after a crafty return of serve.
annotation.walkthrough: Passing shot and return are tennis terms, so the whole clue reads as a rally; 'shot' and 'returns' are really instructions.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a passing phase is transient, lasting only a short time.
